Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET503 Module 1
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Grashof's Law: $s + l \le p + q$ (Shortest + Longest $\le$ sum of other two links)
  • Degrees of Freedom (Kutzbach): $DOF = 3(n - 1) - 2j - h$ (Planar mechanisms)
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Four-Bar Inversions: Crank-Rocker (shortest fixed), Double-Crank (shortest adjacent), Double-Rocker (shortest opposite).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • If $s + l > p + q$, all inversions are double-rocker mechanisms.

Module 2.title: Velocity, Acceleration & Coriolis Acceleration
Module 2.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Coriolis Component of Acceleration</text><text x='130' y='75' fill='#ef4444' font-size='16' font-weight='bold'>a_c = 2 · ω · v (Slider on Rotating Link)</text></svg>
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET503 Module 2
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Coriolis Acceleration: $a_c = 2 \omega v$ (Direction found by rotating sliding velocity vector $v$ by $90^\circ$ in sense of $\omega$)
  • Aronhold-Kennedy Theorem: Three bodies in relative motion have their three instantaneous centers collinear.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Centripetal vs Tangential Acceleration: $a_r = \omega^2 r = v^2/r$ (radial towards center); $a_t = \alpha r$ (tangential).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Coriolis acceleration exists ONLY when a slider moves along a link that is simultaneously rotating.

Module 3.title: Cam Profiles & Follower Dynamics
Module 3.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Cam Follower Motion Profile (SHM)</text><text x='90' y='75' fill='#fcd34d' font-size='14'>Displacement: y = (h/2) · [1 - cos(πθ/β)]</text></svg>
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET503 Module 3
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • SHM Follower Motion: $y = \frac{h}{2}\left(1 - \cos\frac{\pi\theta}{\beta}\right)$, Max velocity $v_{\max} = \frac{\pi h \omega}{2\beta}$, Max acceleration $a_{\max} = \frac{\pi^2 h \omega^2}{2\beta^2}$
  • Pressure Angle ($\alpha$): Angle between follower motion axis and normal to pitch curve (Keep $\alpha \le 30^\circ$ to prevent jamming).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Cycloidal Motion: Zero jerk at boundaries; best for high-speed automated machinery.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Base circle is the smallest circle tangent to the cam profile.

Module 4.title: Flywheels & Turning Moment Diagrams
Module 4.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Flywheel Turning Moment Dynamics</text><text x='110' y='75' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='15'>ΔE = I · ω_avg² · C_s = m · k² · ω_avg² · C_s</text></svg>
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET503 Module 4
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Maximum Fluctuation of Energy: $\Delta E = E_{\max} - E_{\min} = I \omega_{\text{mean}}^2 C_s$
  • Coefficient of Fluctuation of Speed ($C_s$): $C_s = \frac{\omega_1 - \omega_2}{\omega_{\text{mean}}} = \frac{2(N_1 - N_2)}{N_1 + N_2}$
  • Flywheel Mass Calculation: $m = \frac{\Delta E}{k^2 \omega^2 C_s}$ (where $k$ is radius of gyration)
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Flywheel vs Governor: Flywheel smooths cyclic torque fluctuations within one cycle; Governor adjusts fuel flow to regulate speed across varying external loads.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Flywheel stores kinetic energy when engine torque exceeds load torque.

Module 5.title: Balancing of Rotating & Reciprocating Masses
Module 5.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px; margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Reciprocating Unbalanced Inertia Forces</text><text x='80' y='75' fill='#ef4444' font-size='14'>F_p = m · r · ω² · cos(θ) • F_s = m · r · ω² · (cos 2θ / n)</text></svg>
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MET503 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Centrifugal Force: $F_c = m r \omega^2$
  • Dynamic Balancing Conditions: Both force polygon ($\sum \mathbf{F} = 0$) and couple polygon ($\sum \mathbf{C} = 0$) must close.
  • Primary Unbalanced Force: $F_p = m r \omega^2 \cos\theta$ (at engine speed $\omega$)
  • Secondary Unbalanced Force: $F_s = m r \omega^2 \frac{\cos 2\theta}{n}$ (at twice engine speed $2\omega$)
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Partial Balancing of Reciprocating Masses: Balancing fraction $c$ ($0.5-0.67$) creates unbalanced transverse shaking force $(1-c)mr\omega^2\sin\theta$ (swaying couple, hammer blow).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Complete dynamic balance of rotating masses in different planes requires at least TWO balancing masses in two reference planes.
